text:
The tool output doesn't confirm that Sentinel-2 imagery was used. The 2022 loss comes from the Hansen/UMD Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13), an annual series covering 2001–2025 at 30 m pixel size. That pixel size is typical of Landsat-derived products, not Sentinel-2's 10 m resolution. The tool output doesn't list the underlying sensor, though, so I can't say what imagery fed the dataset.

What the evidence does show:
- Loss of 0.6 ha in 2022, about 3.41% of the 17.6 ha asset.
- The JRC 2020 reference maps 100% of the event area as forest.
- A later year was observed (up to 2025), so the corroboration rule is met.
- The MGAP 2021 map classes 0.5 ha as native forest and 0.1 ha as outside mapped forest.

No Sentinel-2 dataset appears among the sources used.
